title: Geriatrician visit
what: A doctor for older people looks at your health as a whole: memory, balance, mood and medicines. They help you stay independent.
why: For people over 65 to 70 with several illnesses at once, falls, worsening memory or many medicines.
duration: the visit usually takes 40 to 60 minutes
tell_doctor: All your medicines, including supplements and herbs
Changes in memory, mood or sleep

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Put all the packages in a bag and bring them. The doctor will check how they work together.

prepare.title: Companion
prepare.text: It is best to come with a close person who knows about your health and daily life.

prepare.title: Questions
prepare.text: Write down in advance what worries you most.

bring: All your medicines in their packages
Glasses and a hearing aid, if you have them
steps: The doctor asks in detail about your health and daily life
Does simple tests of memory and balance
Measures your blood pressure and weight
Makes a plan: treatment, exercises and help at home
feel: The tests are simple, sometimes tiring - you can ask for a break
after: The doctor may stop or replace some medicines - do not change them yourself
At home, remove things you could trip over
Come back for a follow-up when your doctor says
red_flags: Sudden weakness in an arm or leg, a drooping face or trouble speaking - call your local emergency number
Sudden confusion - call your local emergency number

faq.q: Why a geriatrician if I have a general doctor?
faq.a: A geriatrician sees everything together and helps sort out many medicines and problems.

faq.q: Can a relative come without the older person?
faq.a: They can ask for advice, but the patient needs to be examined in person. Ask the clinic.

reminders.text: Geriatrician visit tomorrow. Put all your medicines in a bag and take your medical summaries.
